message.abstract: <jats:p>Throughout this paper <jats:italic>q</jats:italic><jats:sub>1</jats:sub>,<jats:italic>q</jats:italic><jats:sub>2</jats:sub>,… are positive and <jats:italic>x</jats:italic><jats:sub>1</jats:sub>,<jats:italic>x</jats:italic><jats:sub>2</jats:sub>,… non-negative real numbers. When <jats:italic>q</jats:italic><jats:sub>1</jats:sub>+…+ <jats:italic>q</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>n</jats:italic></jats:sub> = 1, we define Δ<jats:sub><jats:italic>n</jats:italic></jats:sub>, <jats:italic>S</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>n</jats:italic></jats:sub> and Σ<jats:sub><jats:italic>n</jats:italic></jats:sub> as follows:</jats:p><jats:p><jats:disp-formula><jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" mimetype="image" position="float" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0305004100036963_eqn001"/></jats:disp-formula></jats:p><jats:p><jats:disp-formula><jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" mimetype="image" position="float" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0305004100036963_eqn002"/></jats:disp-formula></jats:p><jats:p>and</jats:p><jats:p><jats:disp-formula><jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" mimetype="image" position="float" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0305004100036963_eqn003"/></jats:disp-formula></jats:p><jats:p>We use the term ‘comparable’ in Kober's(2) sense. Two functions <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>(<jats:italic>x</jats:italic><jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, …, <jats:italic>x<jats:sub>n</jats:sub></jats:italic>) and <jats:italic>g</jats:italic>(<jats:italic>x</jats:italic><jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, …, <jats:italic>x<jats:sub>n</jats:sub></jats:italic>) are comparable if and only if α<jats:italic>g</jats:italic> ≤ <jats:italic>f</jats:italic> ≤ β<jats:italic>g</jats:italic> for some positive constants α and β.</jats:p>
